AdelicAlgebraicGroups.summary: Mathlib's Topology/Algebra/RestrictedProduct/ gives the whole topological half of AA.0 in full generality: topological-group and topological-ring instances, local compactness over compact open subgroups, the open-embedding/cylinder lemmas and continuity criteria for maps in and out. For the adelic layers the libraries supply the G_a and G_m cases and some algebraic scaffolding: the adele ring, idele group and idele class group, the product formula, discreteness and closedness of K in its adele ring (Tau Ceti), Tau Ceti's functor of points of an affine group scheme — so G(𝔸) exists as an abstract group, compatibly with products, but with no topology — Kˣ-valued weak approximation, and strong approximation for SL₂ over ℚ in its congruence form (SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ) surjective). On the measure side Mathlib has quotient measures, independence of the fundamental domain and the unfolding formula for countable subgroups, and Weil's integration formula for a closed normal subgroup (Haar/Extension.lean), but no measure on a restricted product or on the adeles, no invariant measure on H\G for a non-normal closed subgroup, and no Tamagawa measure. Genuinely missing: the topological group G(𝔸) and its functoriality, unimodularity, a_G and H_G, all of reduction theory (rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite volume, compactness criteria, class-number finiteness), approximation for general groups, level maps and Hecke diagrams, and the AA.5 comparisons beyond the definition of the idele class group.

targets.target: Restricted product of topological groups: continuity of multiplication and inversion
targets.note: Proved for Πʳ i, [R i, B i] with each R i a topological group and each B i an *open* subgroup (hypothesis `Fact (∀ i, IsOpen (B i))`, spelled `hBopen`); the anonymous `ContinuousMul` instance just above line 606 supplies continuity of multiplication. No sorry in the file.

targets.target: Local compactness of the restricted product
targets.note: Exactly the layer's hypotheses: each R i locally compact, B i an open subgroup, and B i compact for all but finitely many i. The weakly-locally-compact versions do not even need the group structure.

targets.target: Compact-open cylinders: the level subgroups are open and carry the subspace topology
targets.note: `isOpen_forall_mem` says {x | ∀ i, x i ∈ C i} is open for opens C i with C i = A i cofinitely; with `isOpenEmbedding_structureMap` this is the compact-open cylinder basis. The topology is the colimit over finite exceptional sets (`topologicalSpace_eq_iSup`).

targets.target: Continuity criteria for homomorphisms into and out of a restricted product
targets.note: `continuous_dom` reduces continuity on the source to continuity on each level piece; `mapAlong_continuous` gives continuity of index-changing maps, which is the functoriality criterion the layer wants.

targets.target: Restricted product of Haar measures normalized so that the chosen compact opens have volume one at almost all places
targets.note: grep for `measur` in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/RestrictedProduct/*.lean, Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/AdeleRing.lean and the Tau Ceti adele files returns nothing: no MeasurableSpace or Measure is put on a restricted product or on the adeles. `infinitePi` builds an infinite product only of *probability* measures on the full product, which is the nearest technical input.

targets.target: Change-of-finite-set and Fubini statements for the product measure
targets.note: Mathlib has full Fubini for finite products and for infinite products of probability measures, and `infinitePi_map_restrict` is the change-of-finite-set statement in that setting; what is missing is any of this for a restricted product of Haar measures, since the measure itself does not exist.

targets.target: Tamagawa measures with convergence factors, distinguished from normalized product measures
targets.note: `grep -rn -i tamagawa` over both trees returns nothing, and there is no convergence-factor construction anywhere.

duplicates.note: Also builds the restricted product from local completions and valuation rings and proves local compactness, in the function-field case; the elementary restricted-product lemmas are the same statements.
Defines restricted products from curve places with integral orders and compatible Haar measures, i.e. the function-field version of AA.0's normalized product Haar measure.
Constructs the restricted product of local metaplectic covers with splittings over almost all maximal compacts, reusing the same restricted-product-of-locally-compact-groups machinery.

targets.target: Independence of the spreading-out model and of the finite exceptional set for G(A)
targets.note: Changing the finite exceptional set is available abstractly for restricted products, but there is no smooth affine model of an algebraic group over O_S and hence no statement that G(A) is independent of the model.

targets.target: The adelic points functor G ↦ G(A) with the diagonal G(F) → G(A) and local projections
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor` sends every commutative R-algebra A to the convolution group of A-points of the affine group scheme of a Hopf algebra, functorially in A. Evaluated on the adele ring it gives the abstract group G(𝔸), and `mapPoints` along K → 𝔸[K] gives the diagonal; the local projections still need 𝔸[K] → K_v packaged as algebra maps (only ring homomorphisms such as `evalRingHom` exist). For GL_n and G_m Tau Ceti identifies the points with GL_n(A) and Aˣ. Missing: any topology on G(𝔸), its identification with the restricted product of the G(F_v) with respect to G(O_v) for a model over O_S, and hence the adelic group itself. For G_a and G_m the adelic objects do exist concretely: the adele ring with its diagonal, and IdeleGroup = 𝔸ˣ, which `unitsEquiv` identifies with the restricted product of the local unit groups (as groups only).

targets.target: Base change and restriction-of-scalars equivalences on adelic points
targets.note: Base change on points is algebraically available: `baseChangePointsMulEquiv` identifies (A →ₐ[k] R) with (K ⊗ A →ₐ[K] R) as convolution groups for any K-algebra R. But there is no Weil restriction in either tree (`grep -rn -i 'weil restriction'` finds only prose), no map 𝔸_F → 𝔸_E or identification 𝔸_E ≅ E ⊗_F 𝔸_F, and no topology on adelic points, so neither Res_{E/F} G(𝔸_F) ≅ G(𝔸_E) nor the adelic base-change equivalence can be stated.

targets.target: Compatibility of adelic points with closed subgroups, centres and products
targets.note: On points all three compatibilities hold for every commutative value algebra, so for 𝔸 as abstract groups: points of a product are the product of the points (`pointsMulEquiv`, natural in the algebra), points of the closed subgroup cut out by a Hopf ideal are the points vanishing on it (`quotientPointsSubgroup`), and over a field the points of the centre (`centerDefiningIdeal`) are the universally central points (`centerPointsSubgroup_eq_center`). Missing: everything topological — that H(𝔸) → G(𝔸) is a closed embedding, that the product decomposition is a homeomorphism — since G(𝔸) carries no topology in either library.

targets.target: G(F) is a discrete subgroup of G(A) (and not of the finite adeles alone)
targets.note: Proved without sorry for the additive group: K is discrete and closed in 𝔸[K], and 𝔸[K]/K is T3. The layer's caveat is not a theorem anywhere: density of K in the finite adele ring appears only in the docstring of Tau Ceti's Discrete.lean (it is planned as `denseRange_algebraMap_finiteAdeleRing` in the GlobalNumberFields roadmap), and the cited `InfiniteAdeleRing.denseRange_algebraMap` is density in the infinite adele ring K∞, i.e. weak approximation at the archimedean places. Nothing for a general G.

targets.target: G(A) is unimodular for reductive G
targets.note: Mathlib defines the modular character of a locally compact group, so unimodularity is expressible (∆ ≡ 1), but there is no Haar measure on any adelic group and no such theorem.

duplicates.note: Its own text says it consumes AA.0–AA.1 for adelic topological points and restriction-of-scalars point comparisons, so the two layers state overlapping functoriality targets.
Owns Weil restriction for affine finite-type schemes; AA.1's restriction-of-scalars equivalence on adelic points is the adelic shadow of that construction.

targets.target: The real character space a_G = Hom(X*_F(G), R) and the logarithmic map H_G
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the geometric character lattice X*(G_Fbar) with its Galois action (so F-rational characters are the Galois invariants), but not the real vector space a_G, not H_G, and not G(A)^1.

targets.target: Vanishing of H_G on G(F) (product formula)
targets.note: The GL_1 case, the product formula for a number field over all places with the normalized absolute values, is proved in both libraries; the statement for a general F-rational character of G is not.

targets.target: Invariant quotient measures and Weil's integral formula, independent of the fundamental domain
targets.note: Two pieces are in Mathlib. For a countable subgroup acting with a fundamental domain: independence of the fundamental domain (`IsFundamentalDomain.measure_eq`), uniqueness of the quotient measure, Haar-ness of the quotient measure for a normal discrete subgroup, and the unfolding formula. For a closed normal subgroup (via `TopologicalGroup.IsSES.ofClosedSubgroup`), Haar/Extension.lean builds a Haar measure on the group from Haar measures on the subgroup and on the quotient and proves ∫_B f = ∫_C (∫_A f(b·a) da) dc for compactly supported continuous f — Weil's formula in the normal case. Missing: the invariant measure on H\G for a non-normal, non-discrete closed subgroup under the condition Δ_G|_H = Δ_H (needed for quotients such as Z(𝔸)G(F)\G(𝔸) or N(𝔸)\G(𝔸)), and the extension from compactly supported continuous functions to integrable ones.

targets.target: Modulus character of a parabolic from the adjoint action on Lie(N), with its product formula on rational points
targets.note: The abstract modular character ∆_G of a locally compact group and the distributive Haar character of a group acting by automorphisms are both in Mathlib, and Tau Ceti has the Levi decomposition P = L ⋉ N of a dynamic parabolic; but ∆_P computed as |det Ad|_{Lie N}| and its product formula over the places are not stated.

targets.target: Central-character sections and L² spaces with a fixed unitary central character, with change of central quotient
targets.note: Only the general Lp theory exists; there is no L²(Z(A)G(F)\G(A), ω) and no measurable section of a central quotient.

targets.target: Tamagawa measures from invariant differential forms and convergence factors, independent of rescaling by F^×
targets.note: No Tamagawa measure, no invariant differential form on an algebraic group and no convergence factors anywhere in either tree.

duplicates.note: Bloch's Tamagawa reformulation asks for the same adelic/Tamagawa measure description: local measures, their product, and the finite-volume integrals.
Constructs quotient measures on centralizer quotients and the comparison of Haar normalizations, which is AA.2's quotient-measure and normalization target in the orbital-integral setting.
Self-dual Haar measures from a rational differential and the rescaling identity are the function-field analogue of AA.2's differential-form Tamagawa measure and its F^×-rescaling independence.

targets.target: Minimal rational parabolic subgroups and relative positive chambers
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the dynamic parabolic P(λ) of a cocharacter with its Levi decomposition, and root-system chambers in LinearAlgebra/RootSystem, but no relative (F-rational) root system, no minimality theorem and no relative positive chamber.

targets.target: Siegel sets and their height estimates
targets.note: `grep -i siegel` in the declaration index finds only Siegel's lemma on small integer solutions (Mathlib/NumberTheory/SiegelsLemma.lean) and `NumberField.house.asiegel`; nothing about Siegel sets in a reductive group.

targets.target: Finitely many Siegel sets cover the arithmetic quotient; finite intersection property
targets.note: Absent, as is the Siegel set itself.

targets.target: Finite volume of G(F)\G(A)^1
targets.note: Covolume of a discrete subgroup is defined in Mathlib and finiteness is available once a finite-measure fundamental domain is exhibited, but G(A)^1 does not exist and there is no Haar measure on an adelic group.

targets.target: Compactness of the quotient for F-anisotropic groups modulo centre, and the converse
targets.note: Absent; not even the additive statement (compactness of 𝔸[K]/K) is in the libraries, although the Tau Ceti Discrete.lean docstring refers to it.

targets.target: Moderate-growth estimates under change of faithful representation and of maximal compact subgroup
targets.note: No height/growth function on an adelic group is defined.

targets.target: Finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K modulo the archimedean connected component (class-number finiteness)
targets.note: Only the GL_1 shadow exists: finiteness of the ideal class group of a number field. The general adelic double-coset finiteness is absent.

duplicates.note: Explicitly consumes rational parabolics, Siegel sets, finite arithmetic coverings and adelic component finiteness, and restates the component-decomposition consequence.

Imports restriction of scalars, Haar/Tamagawa measures and reduction theory from this roadmap and specializes them to orders in central division algebras; the hidden readiness checkpoint KU-arithmeticgroups previously cited here only aggregates R.1.
States rapid decay on Siegel sets, which presupposes and partly restates the Siegel-set construction and height estimates of AA.3.
Proves compactness of the norm-one idele class group and recovers class-group finiteness from it: the GL₁ case of AA.3's finite volume of G(F)\G(A)¹ and finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K.

targets.target: Weak approximation for algebraic groups, in the justified cases, with visible failure for tori
targets.note: Only field-level statements are proved: K is dense in every finite product of its completions (G_a), and a single element of Kˣ approximates targets at finitely many finite places while taking prescribed signs at the real places (the G_m form). Nothing for a general algebraic group, and no discussion of the failure of weak approximation for tori.

targets.target: Strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple G outside S with a noncompact local factor
targets.note: The one algebraic-group case is SL₂ over ℚ with S = {∞}, in congruence form: Tau Ceti proves SL₂(ℤ) → SL₂(ℤ/dℤ) surjective for every d, jointly at two coprime moduli, which is equivalent to density of SL₂(ℤ) in SL₂(ℤ̂). It is not stated adelically, and nothing covers other simply connected groups or other number fields; even additive strong approximation for a number field (density of K in the finite adeles) is unproved. Tau Ceti also proves strong approximation for the field of a function field. It has simply connected algebraic groups (Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/SimplyConnected), but no approximation theorem uses them.

targets.target: Finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels, and degrees via stabilizer indices
targets.note: The abstract ingredients exist: for H ≤ G acting on E with E → E/G a quotient covering map, E/H → E/G is a covering map (`isCoveringMap_of_comp`), and the degree of a double coset H₁gH₂ is the index [H₁ : H₁ ∩ gH₂g⁻¹] (`degree_eq_relIndex`). No neatness predicate exists in either library — the word occurs only in three informal comments — and there are no adelic level quotients G(F)\G(𝔸)/K whose covering degrees could be computed.

targets.target: Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences on adelic quotients
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a classical Hecke ring for GL_2 and GL_n double cosets (TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/), but no adelic double-coset correspondence with Cartesian squares of level covers.

targets.target: Quotient groupoids and stabilizers in the non-neat case
targets.note: No algebraic-stack quotient of an adelic double-coset space exists in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves existence of neat congruence subgroups and uses strong approximation in the same restricted form, so the neatness and approximation targets overlap.
Owns additive strong approximation and the idele group; AA.4's approximation targets are the algebraic-group generalization of that layer.

targets.target: Identification of the GL_1 adelic quotient with the idele class group, and the split-centre normalization with the norm-one subgroup
targets.note: The idele class group 𝔸ˣ/Kˣ is defined in Mathlib (as an abbrev, with no structure theory), and the product formula shows the principal ideles have norm one; but the norm-one idele subgroup 𝔸^1, its compactness modulo Kˣ, and the comparison with the GL_1 case of a general adelic quotient are all missing.

targets.target: Identification of the GL_2/Q component with the upper half-plane
targets.note: Mathlib and Tau Ceti have the upper half-plane with its SL(2,R) action and modular curves at level Γ(N), but no adelic GL_2(A) description and hence no comparison.

targets.target: Compactness of the quotient for a definite quaternion inner form
targets.note: Quaternion algebras exist in Mathlib (Mathlib/Algebra/Quaternion.lean) but there is no adelic group of a quaternion algebra and no compactness statement.

targets.target: Comparison of volumes under finite-index level changes
targets.note: Mathlib has both shapes of the wanted statement: [G:H]·μ(H) = μ(G) for a measurable finite-index subgroup and a left-invariant measure (`Subgroup.index_mul_measure`, the local identity vol(K) = [K:K']·vol(K')), and the covolume/index relation for ℤ-lattices in a real vector space. There is no measure on an adelic group and hence no volume of an adelic quotient to compare.

duplicates.note: Owns level structures and the quotient identification that AA.5 imports for the GL_2/Q comparison.
Its connected-component decomposition is the same identification of an adelic double-coset quotient with a classical arithmetic quotient.

Defines the idele norm, the closed norm-one subgroup IdeleClassGroup.normOne and proves its compactness, recording that the full idele class group is not compact: the GL_1 split-centre normalization AA.5 identifies.

AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights.summary: Both libraries have a rich analytic theory of modular forms on the upper half-plane: Mathlib's ModularForm/CuspForm with slash actions, cusps, q-expansions and the injectivity of the q-expansion map, the Serre derivative, level-one dimension formulas and Eisenstein series; Tau Ceti adds Hecke operators for Γ₀(N)/Γ₁(N) with nebentypus, eigenforms, the old/new decomposition, Atkin–Lehner, multiplicity one, the Sturm bound, finite-dimensionality for any finite-index subgroup and the freeness of E₄, E₆ as generators of the level-one graded ring. None of the algebraic side of this roadmap exists: no modular curve as a scheme, no Hodge bundle or cusp divisor, no modular form over a coefficient ring or in characteristic p, no Hasse invariant, characteristic-p theta operator or Igusa curve, no Galois representation attached to an eigenform or residual semisimplification, no tame inertia characters or finite-flat local Galois theory, and no Serre weight k(ρ̄) or level N(ρ̄). Tau Ceti does supply two carriers the local recipe will need — finite locally free commutative group schemes with Cartier duality, and the Kummer map into continuous H¹(G_K, μₙ) for any field — and Mathlib supplies the commutative algebra (going-down, minimal primes, DVR lifting) behind the Deligne–Serre lemma. The genuinely missing work is essentially the whole roadmap.

targets.target: The Hodge bundle omega on a modular curve
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'hodge bundle'` over both trees returns nothing, and no modular curve exists as a scheme or stack in either library.

targets.target: Cusp ideal / cusp divisor on the compactified curve
targets.note: Only the analytic cusp is present (the cusp function of a periodic form, and `Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean` for the set of cusps); there is no cusp divisor on an algebraic curve.

targets.target: Geometric modular forms as sections of omega^k, and their base change along a ring map
targets.note: Mathlib's `ModularForm Γ k` is a complex-analytic function on the upper half-plane; there is no space of forms over a general base ring and hence nothing to base change.

targets.target: Agreement of geometric and analytic forms over C (GAGA comparison)
targets.note: `grep -rn -i gaga` over both trees returns nothing: there is no analytification functor or GAGA theorem in either library.

targets.target: Coefficient-field and integral q-expansion comparison via the moduli family
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the universal Weierstrass curve over Z[a_1,...,a_6] and its specialization property, which is the closest thing to a universal family, but it is not a family over a modular curve and carries no level structure.

targets.target: Descent for small levels from a rigidified cover or the moduli stack, with stabilisers visible
targets.note: No algebraic stack of elliptic curves and no level structures on a family exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Owns the Hodge bundle and the identification of weight-two cusp forms with regular differentials, which is the case k=2 of R15.1's construction and comparison.
Identifies the characteristic-zero Hodge bundle after extension to a splitting field and proves descent, the Hilbert analogue of R15.1.
Constructs the determinant of invariant differentials (the Hodge bundle) of an abelian scheme, the general case of the same bundle.
Owns projective coherent GAGA, the equivalence of coherent algebraic and analytic sheaves on a projective complex scheme, which is the GAGA step of R15.1's comparison of geometric and analytic forms.

targets.target: q-expansion principle: a form is detected by its q-expansions at the needed cusps
targets.note: Mathlib proves the analytic statement at the cusp at infinity: for Γ ≤ GL(2,R) with a strict period h > 0, f ↦ qExpansion h f is injective on ModularForm Γ k. This is one cusp, over C, for connected-type Γ; the geometric statement (a section of omega^k over a base ring vanishing iff its q-expansion vanishes) is absent.

targets.target: Integral version of the q-expansion principle
targets.note: No forms over a ring exist, so there is no integral q-expansion principle and no bounded-denominator statement.

targets.target: Finite generation and base change of spaces of forms
targets.note: Over ℂ only: Tau Ceti proves M_k(Γ) and S_k(Γ) finite-dimensional for any finite-index Γ ≤ SL(2,ℤ) (via the Sturm bound) and that E₄ and E₆ freely generate the graded ring of level-one forms (`mvPolynomialEquivModularForms`); Mathlib has the level-one dimension formula. Finite generation of modules of forms over a coefficient ring, and its compatibility with base change, do not exist.

targets.target: Hecke actions and the coefficient formulas for their q-expansions
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the full analytic Hecke theory for Γ_0(N) with nebentypus: T_n on q-expansions, the eigenvalue/coefficient identity a_n(f) = λ_n a_1(f), the old/new decomposition and multiplicity one. The layer wants the Hecke action defined from the algebraic correspondences of R14 and *compared* with this; the algebraic side does not exist.

targets.target: Algebraic integrality of Hecke eigenvalues and their reduction
targets.note: No statement that the eigenvalues of a normalised eigenform are algebraic integers, and no reduction of a q-expansion modulo a prime, appears in either library (`grep -i` for IsIntegral/𝓞 in the Tau Ceti ModularForms tree finds only unrelated uses).

targets.target: Separation of reduction of characteristic-zero forms from lifting a characteristic-p eigenform
targets.note: There are no characteristic-p modular forms at all, so neither direction is stated.

duplicates.note: Proves the formal comparison at the Tate curve 'used in the q-expansion principle', i.e. the geometric input to R15.2's first target.
Also asks for the q-expansion principle together with integral level structures and diamond operators, for the ordinary tower.
Owns the integral Hecke algebra, coefficient fields and the integral q-expansions-at-all-cusps lattice argument, which is exactly R15.2's integral Hecke theory.
Builds an integral q-expansion principle for Hilbert Eisenstein series; the same principle in a wider setting.

targets.target: The Hasse invariant with its q-expansion
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'hasse invariant'` and `hasseInvariant` over both trees return nothing: Mathlib's Hasse names are the Hasse derivative and the Hasse diagram, and the quadratic-form Hasse invariant exists only as a Tau Ceti roadmap target. There is also no supersingular/ordinary theory or [p]-series height; the inputs to E_{p−1} ≡ 1 (mod p) — the Eisenstein q-expansion coefficients and von Staudt–Clausen — are in Mathlib but the congruence is not stated.

targets.target: Frobenius and Verschiebung on forms in characteristic p
targets.note: Frobenius and Verschiebung exist for Witt vectors and (in Tau Ceti) Frobenius isogenies of elliptic curves in TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/EllipticCurve/Isogeny/Frobenius, but not as operators on mod-p modular forms.

targets.target: The theta operator with its q-expansion formula and Hecke compatibility
targets.note: Mathlib has the normalized derivative D = (2πi)⁻¹ d/dz of a complex modular form and the Serre derivative D − (k/12)E₂ as a map M_k(Γ) → M_{k+2}(Γ) for Γ ≤ SL(2,ℤ) (`serreDerivativeMF`), but no q-expansion formula a_n(Df) = n·a_n(f), no Hecke compatibility and nothing in characteristic p, where θ = q d/dq preserves mod-p forms.

targets.target: Filtration and weight-change results with exact hypotheses on p and level, including p = 2, 3
targets.note: No mod-p filtration of a modular form exists.

targets.target: The Igusa-curve interpretation
targets.note: `grep -rn -i igusa` over both trees returns nothing.

duplicates.note: Proves the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem 'with its characteristic-p operations', so it restates the theta/filtration package of R15.3.
Uses Hasse sections and the ample Hasse invariant on strata, the higher-dimensional version of R15.3's Hasse invariant.

targets.target: Serre's piecewise weight recipe k(rho-bar) as an exhaustive local case table
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'serre weight'` returns nothing in either tree; there is no residual Galois representation to feed the recipe.

targets.target: Tame inertia characters and the irreducible local-inertia case
targets.note: Mathlib has decomposition/inertia subgroups in Hilbert ramification theory and the p-adic cyclotomic character of a field with enough roots of unity, but no fundamental tame characters of level 1 and 2 and no local Galois representation theory.

targets.target: Reducible local representations: scalar and extension-sensitive cases, with the extension class stored
targets.note: Tau Ceti has continuous H¹ of the absolute Galois group of any field in low degree, and the Kummer map Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ ↪ H¹(G_K, μₙ) (`kummerClassMap_injective`; surjectivity via Hilbert 90 is not yet there), which for K = ℚ_p contains the classes Serre's peu/très ramifié condition is phrased in. Missing: the identification of H¹ with extensions of characters, two-dimensional local Galois representations, the peu ramifié notion and any storage of an extension class with the recipe.

targets.target: Twisting and determinant parity of the recipe
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Invariance of the weight under coefficient extension and isomorphism
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: For p = 2: weight 2 exactly in the finite-flat case, weight 4 otherwise
targets.note: The finite-flat condition on a local representation (ρ̄|G_{ℚ₂} prolongs to a finite flat group scheme over ℤ₂) cannot be stated: neither library attaches group schemes to Galois modules or has Raynaud or Fontaine–Laffaille theory. Tau Ceti does have finite locally free commutative affine group schemes over any commutative ring, with Cartier duality (`FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDuality`) and its base change — the carrier such a condition would use.

duplicates.note: Titled 'Local residual types and Serre weights'; derives the inertia characters of elliptic-curve torsion, the local input R15.4 says it depends on, with overlapping statements.
Proves the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem including the reducible and irreducible local cases, i.e. the same case table used as an optimisation theorem.
States the level-one theorem 'with its classical Serre weight' for every residual characteristic, so it restates the recipe.
Constructs tame characters and the fundamental characters of levels one and two, the inertia characters in which Serre's recipe for the irreducible local case is written.

targets.target: The Deligne–Serre eigenvalue-lifting lemma for a finite Hecke algebra
targets.note: The commutative-algebra ingredients (minimal primes, going-down for flat algebras, DVR lifting) are in Mathlib, but the lemma itself — a mod-p eigensystem of a finite torsion-free O-algebra lifts to a characteristic-zero eigensystem after extending O — is nowhere stated, in either library.

targets.target: Application to the relevant modular-form modules
targets.note: Tau Ceti's Hecke algebra acts on complex spaces of cusp forms with multiplicity one, but there is no integral Hecke algebra acting on a lattice of forms and no mod-p eigensystem to lift.

targets.target: Passage from a mod-p eigensystem at controlled weight and level to a characteristic-zero normalised eigenform, with the possible weight change
targets.note: Absent; there are no characteristic-p eigenforms.

targets.target: Special low weights, including Katz weight one
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Constructs the weight-one Artin representation 'in the Deligne–Serre setting', consuming and restating R15.5's lifting.
Its sublayer 8W routes through Deligne–Serre 1974 Prop 2.7, the same lifting argument.
Organizes Deligne–Serre Artin representations and weight-one modularity, overlapping the same lifting statement.

targets.target: Residual modularity: coefficient field, prime over p, eigenform and isomorphism with the residual semisimplification
targets.note: There is no Galois representation attached to an eigenform in either library, and no semisimplification of a representation over a finite field; `grep -i semisimplification` in the declaration index returns nothing.

targets.target: The classical weight-and-level target stated with N(rho-bar) and k(rho-bar)
targets.note: Neither invariant is defined.

targets.target: Elementary character/determinant congruence consequences of the local recipe
targets.note: The mod-p cyclotomic character is available as the reduction of Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter, but the congruence det rho-bar = chi^{k-1} eps is not stated.

targets.target: Finite-flat weight-two consequence
targets.note: Absent, as is finite-flat local theory.

ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces.summary: The geometry this roadmap needs is absent: there is no Cartan involution, maximal compact subgroup or symmetric space of a real reductive group, no arithmetic quotient, Borel–Serre compactification, singular or compact-support cohomology, cup product, Poincaré–Lefschetz duality, Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, perfect complex or lim¹. What exists is infrastructure: Mathlib's ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul with finite stabilizers (with instances for discrete subgroups of SL(2,ℝ) and arithmetic subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) acting on ℍ), CW complexes, singular homology with homotopy invariance, spectral objects and derived categories, and group cohomology with Shapiro's lemma and degree-one inflation–restriction; Tau Ceti adds relative singular homology of pairs and triples, local coefficient systems as functors on the fundamental groupoid with their monodromy, the classification of covering spaces by fundamental-groupoid actions, continuous degree-one inflation–restriction and — most substantially — the abstract Hecke ring of a double-coset triple, proved associative (and commutative under an anti-involution). The prerequisite Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology roadmap plans cellular homology, transfer for finite covers, singular cochains with local coefficients, cup products and Poincaré–Lefschetz duality (its stages 4–6), which ALS.1, ALS.3, ALS.5 and ALS.6 should consume rather than rebuild.

Absent: the statement for an arithmetic subgroup of a general G(F_∞) acting on its symmetric space, and freeness at neat level (there is no neatness predicate in either library; the word occurs only in informal comments).

AutomorphicBundles.summary: This roadmap lives on Shimura varieties, and neither library has one: there is no Shimura datum, canonical model, compact dual, Hermitian symmetric domain, toroidal or minimal compactification, automorphic vector bundle, canonical principal bundle or canonical/subcanonical extension, and no Hilbert, Siegel or unitary modular form. The classical end fares better: Mathlib has the automorphy factor with its cocycle identity, the SlashAction class with the right-action law proved for GL(2,ℝ), SlashInvariantForm, and ModularForm/CuspForm defined by boundedness and vanishing at all cusps, with q-expansions at a cusp and their injectivity; Tau Ceti and Mathlib together have the abstract double-coset Hecke ring, proved associative and unital, which B5 composes against. Tau Ceti also has inputs that are not yet the constructions: fppf quotient torsors, Galois descent for representations, Schur functors for classical groups, local coefficient systems on topological spaces, pure and mixed Hodge structures with polarizations and period-domain points, finite toric fans with subdivisions, and the balanced product of a covering with a discrete set. So B4 has a real classical carrier for its GL₂ cocycle target, B4 and B5 have analytic counterparts of their GL₂ comparison targets, and B0–B3 and the three general-data interfaces are untouched.

targets.target: Generic associated-bundle construction for a torsor and a representation, with tensor products, duals, determinants and pullback
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves that the fppf quotient by a normal subgroup is a torsor (pullback square), but there is no contracted product P ×^G V of a torsor under a group scheme with a representation, and no associated-bundle functor with tensor products, duals, determinants or pullback. The only balanced product is topological with discrete fibre: `TauCeti.BalancedProduct` forms E ×_G A for a quotient covering map and a discrete G-set A and proves it is a covering space.

targets.target: Geometric/analytic descent comparison for the canonical automorphic torsors
targets.note: Absent: there is no analytification of a scheme and no GAGA in either library.

targets.target: Equivariant-function description of sections, in a fixed left/right convention
targets.note: For GL_2 over ℝ the equivariant-function picture is exactly Mathlib's SlashInvariantForm: functions on ℍ transforming by the weight-k automorphy factor, with the right-action law `f ∣[k] (g * h) = (f ∣[k] g) ∣[k] h` (the `slash_mul` law of the SlashAction class, proved for GL(2,ℝ) by the instance at SlashActions.lean:130). Nothing of this is tied to a torsor or generalized to other groups.

targets.target: Representations over coefficient extensions with semilinear descent data
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Galois descent for a representation base-changed along a Galois extension (invariants recover the original span), which is an ingredient, but no descent datum on an automorphic coefficient.

targets.target: Equivariant bundles on the compact dual, the homogeneous Hodge torsor over the complex domain, and the descended analytic bundle at neat level
targets.note: Mathlib has the Grassmannian functor, but there is no flag variety G/P as a scheme, no compact dual and no Hermitian symmetric domain.

targets.target: Exact criterion for a coefficient to descend through the ineffective central subgroup or a finite coarse quotient
targets.note: Only the analytic GL₂ shadow exists: the quotient of ℍ by a properly discontinuous action is a Hausdorff space, Mathlib proves M_k(Γ) = 0 when −1 ∈ Γ and k is odd (the central-subgroup condition), and Tau Ceti proves that a form for Γ' ≤ Γ comes from Γ exactly when it is Γ-slash invariant (`mem_range_ofLeₗ_iff`). There is no algebraic coarse quotient of an arithmetic quotient, no automorphic bundle on one, and no descent criterion for coefficients.

Fixes the associated-bundle convention L_λ = G_C ×_B C_{-λ} on flag manifolds, the compact-dual case of B0's construction.

There is no algebraic de Rham cohomology, no comparison isomorphism, no Hodge tensor or Hodge class, no Mumford–Tate group and no Shimura variety to realize them on.

AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups.summary: Nothing adelic-automorphic is in the libraries: there is no space of automorphic forms, no constant term, no cusp form on a reductive group, no (g,K)-module, Harish-Chandra module or globalization, no relative Lie algebra cohomology or van Est theorem, no Hecke character and no Whittaker or spherical-vector theory. Several ingredients are present and strong. Mathlib has continuous cohomology of any topological group as the homology of the homogeneous continuous-cochain complex, with functoriality and H⁰ = invariants, and Tau Ceti extends it with restriction and inflation in every degree and corestriction, cup products, Shapiro and long exact sequences in low degrees — AF.1a's continuous cochain target. Tau Ceti also has the representation theory of compact groups (Schur orthogonality, unitarizability, characters, isotypic projections and the Peter–Weyl Hilbert basis) and highest-weight theory for split Lie algebras, including the central character χ_λ : Z(U(L)) → K of a weight and the Casimir element; Mathlib has the universal enveloping algebra, compactly supported smooth test functions and Schwartz functions on normed spaces, locally constant functions, and the classical GL₂ modular-form side of the dictionary. What is genuinely missing is everything that joins these: (g,K)-modules and their infinitesimal-character decomposition, relative Lie algebra cochains and van Est, the adelic test-function and moderate-growth calculus, the automorphic space and its constant terms, algebraic-weight rationality, and the GL₁/GL₂ dictionaries.

targets.target: Adelic smooth test functions as a restricted tensor product of locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places and C^infty compactly supported functions at infinity
targets.note: The ingredients exist separately — locally constant functions, compactly supported smooth functions on an open subset of a normed space with their LF topology (`TestFunction`), and the restricted product of sets — but there is no space of smooth functions on a Lie group or a locally profinite group, no restricted tensor product of function spaces and no space of adelic test functions in either library.

targets.target: Height functions from faithful embeddings, with polynomial comparability and translation estimates
targets.note: Mathlib has heights of points over a field with a product formula, but no height function on the adelic points of a group defined from a faithful representation, and no comparability or translation estimate.

targets.target: Independence of the moderate-growth condition from the chosen height
targets.note: Absent; moderate growth is not defined.

targets.target: Uniform moderate growth for all differential operators, and where it follows from admissibility/finiteness
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Differentiation, right translation and the finite Hecke action preserve the specified spaces
targets.note: The abstract Hecke algebra exists in Tau Ceti, but there is no space of adelic functions for it to act on.

duplicates.note: Owns the reduction theory and moderate-growth estimates under change of faithful representation that AF.0's height functions rest on; the growth-estimate targets overlap.
Owns Schwartz–Bruhat functions and Fourier theory on the adeles, the same adelic test-function space.
Constructs compact-level functions and cuspidal subspaces over a function field, restating the same test-function/growth package in that setting.

targets.target: Compatible (g,K)-modules: algebraic infinitesimal action, locally finite K-action, derivative compatibility
targets.note: Tau Ceti has continuous representations of topological groups and Mathlib has Lie modules, but there is no (g,K)-module structure combining them, and no compatibility axiom.

targets.target: U(g_C), its centre action and generalized infinitesimal-character subspaces
targets.note: U(g) with its universal property is in Mathlib and its centre is `Subalgebra.center`. For a split Lie algebra with nondegenerate Killing form in characteristic zero, Tau Ceti constructs the central character χ_λ : Z(U(L)) →ₐ K of a weight from the Verma module, proves that the centre acts through χ_λ on every highest-weight vector of weight λ, and computes χ_λ on the central Casimir element as ⟨λ+ρ,λ+ρ⟩−⟨ρ,ρ⟩; for any algebra it also has the centre acting on a module and the central character of a finite-dimensional simple module over an algebraically closed field (`centralCharacter`). Missing: the Harish-Chandra isomorphism describing Z(U(g)) and when χ_λ = χ_μ, the complexified algebra for a real reductive group, and the decomposition of a (g,K)-module into generalized infinitesimal-character subspaces.

targets.target: Finite K-type multiplicities for admissible modules; locally finite K-action
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Peter–Weyl theorem for a compact group as an explicit Hilbert basis of L^2(G) by normalized matrix coefficients, with Schur orthogonality and unitarizability, sorry-free; this is the decomposition into K-types. Admissibility of a (g,K)-module and finiteness of its K-type multiplicities are not stated because (g,K)-modules do not exist.

targets.target: Smooth moderate-growth Fréchet globalizations of finite-length Harish-Chandra modules, with uniqueness and exactness
targets.note: Absent: `grep -i harishchandra` over both trees returns nothing, and there is no globalization theory.

targets.target: Relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k), V), their differential, functoriality and long exact sequences
targets.note: Mathlib has Lie algebra cochains only in degrees 1 and 2 (with d₁₂, d₂₃ and 2-cocycles, and an explicit TODO for the general Chevalley–Eilenberg complex); the relative complex for a pair (g,K) is absent.

targets.target: Disconnected K handled through its finite component group
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Its pseudocoefficient arguments are said to be constructed 'from AF.1's real representation foundation', so the (g,K)-module targets are shared.
Owns the centre of U(L) and the Harish-Chandra homomorphism, which is AF.1's U(g_C)-centre target.
Also builds the relative Lie algebra cochain complex and identifies it with invariant forms; the cochain construction is stated in both layers.

targets.target: Continuous group-cochain complexes for a real Lie group with finitely many components
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuous cohomology of any topological group with topological coefficients as the homology of the homogeneous continuous-cochain complex, with functoriality and H⁰ = invariants; Tau Ceti adds restriction and inflation in every degree and, on an explicit low-degree model with discrete coefficients, corestriction, cup products of total degree ≤ 2, Shapiro's lemma in degrees 0 and 1 and long exact sequences through degree 2. The complex itself covers a real Lie group with finitely many components. Its cochains are modelled as invariant iterated maps C(G, C(G, …)); their identification with continuous maps on G^{q+1} for locally compact G is a stated Mathlib TODO, which the differentiable-cochain comparison of the next target will need.

targets.target: Differentiable group-cochain complexes and the smoothing comparison
targets.note: Absent: there is no differentiable-cochain complex and no comparison with the continuous one.

targets.target: The complex of G-invariant V-valued differential forms on G/K
targets.note: Mathlib has differential forms with an exterior derivative only on a normed space (Analysis/Calculus/DifferentialForm/Basic.lean); on manifolds Tau Ceti has smooth two-forms (`SmoothTwoForm`) but no forms of other degrees and no exterior derivative, and neither library has the homogeneous space G/K of a Lie group with its invariant forms.

targets.target: Identification of invariant forms with relative Lie algebra cochains, including the finite K/K° action, signs and coefficient action
targets.note: The relative Lie algebra cochain complex does not exist in either library; Mathlib's Lie cochains stop at degree 2.

targets.target: Contracting homotopy on G/K, the relatively injective resolution, and van Est's isomorphism
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'van est'` over both trees returns nothing.

targets.target: Naturality for eligible group/coefficient maps and cup-product compatibility
targets.note: Naturality of continuous cohomology for compatible pairs is in Mathlib in every degree, and Tau Ceti has cup products on continuous cohomology in total degree ≤ 2 on its explicit low-degree model (ContCohomology/Cup), with compatibility with restriction and inflation there. Nothing is stated for van Est maps or the invariant-form complex, which do not exist.

targets.target: Acceptance cases: a compact group by averaging, a real vector group with trivial coefficients, GL_n(C)/U(n), a disconnected group with nontrivial component action
targets.note: Haar averaging over a compact group, which kills higher continuous cohomology, is available in Tau Ceti; the vanishing statement itself and the other three acceptance computations are not in either library.

duplicates.note: Its text says it imports continuous and relative Lie-algebra cochain complexes, van Est and invariant forms from this very stage, so the two state the same targets.
Owns the general continuous-cochain interface (compact/discrete coefficients, derived limits) that this layer's continuous half duplicates for real Lie groups.
Builds continuous cohomology in all degrees on the Mathlib `continuousCohomology` carrier — the same complex, for profinite rather than Lie groups.

targets.target: The space of automorphic forms as an invariant subspace of functions on G(F)\G(A)
targets.note: Absent: there is no adelic quotient of a reductive group in either library.

targets.target: Finite-type/finiteness statements after fixing finite level, a finite set of K-types and an infinitesimal-character ideal
targets.note: Only the classical GL_2 finite-dimensionality of M_k(Γ) is proved (by the Sturm bound); the general finiteness is absent.

targets.target: The Hecke × (g,K) action and the category of automorphic subquotients
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Restricted tensor-product factorization of irreducible admissible constituents
targets.note: Flath's theorem is absent. Tau Ceti has the smoothness condition itself — a discrete module on which every point stabilizer is open (`IsSmoothDiscrete`), equivalent to a discrete continuous module — built for profinite cohomology, but no admissible representations, no restricted tensor product of representations and no factorization theorem.

targets.target: Uniqueness of almost-everywhere spherical vectors up to the specified scalars
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Finiteness (not multiplicity one) of general automorphic multiplicities
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves multiplicity one for classical GL_2 newform eigenspaces, which is the shadow of this in the one case where it holds; the general finiteness statement is absent.

targets.note: Absent; there is no unipotent adelic quotient, no Haar measure on it, and no constant term.

targets.target: Compactness of N(F)\N(A) for the unipotent radical
targets.note: Absent: even the abelian case (compactness of 𝔸/K) is not proved in either library, though Tau Ceti's Discrete.lean docstring refers to it.

targets.target: Convergence, smoothness, equivariance, transitivity for nested parabolics and Hecke compatibility of the constant term
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Cuspidality by vanishing of every proper-parabolic constant term, invariant under conjugacy of parabolics
targets.note: Mathlib's classical cusp form is defined by vanishing at every cusp of Γ, the GL_2 analogue; nothing adelic.

targets.target: Rapid decay on Siegel sets for cusp forms, with the central normalization
targets.note: Mathlib proves exponential decay of a classical cusp form as Im τ → ∞, which is the SL(2,Z) Siegel-set case of the decay statement; there are no Siegel sets in general.

targets.target: Square integrability for unitary central character and finite multiplicity of cuspidal constituents
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Absence of proper rational parabolics for groups anisotropic modulo centre
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines the dynamic parabolic P(λ) of a cocharacter with its Levi and unipotent subgroups, and proves P(λ) = G when the group is commutative (`parabolic_eq_top`). There is no notion of an F-anisotropic reductive group (anisotropy exists only for quadratic forms), no classification of rational parabolics, and no statement that a group anisotropic modulo its centre has no proper rational parabolic.

duplicates.note: Owns the quotient measures and central-character L^2 spaces this layer integrates and concludes in, and AA.3 owns the Siegel sets the decay is stated on.
Constructs constant terms and cuspidal subspaces with their finiteness over a function field — the same targets in that setting.
Builds Arthur's truncation from parabolic constant terms, reusing and restating the constant-term calculus.
Proves K discrete in its adele ring and 𝔸_K/K compact: the case N = G_a of AF.3's compactness of N(F)\N(A), from which the unipotent case follows by filtering N.

targets.target: Algebraic highest weights and their representations
targets.note: Tau Ceti has highest-weight vectors for Lie algebras, Weyl modules and Schur functors for classical groups, and the character lattice of a torus with its Galois action, so algebraic weights have carriers. The automorphic normalization (weights of a reductive group over a number field attached to a representation) is not stated.

targets.target: Infinitesimal characters and cohomological representations
targets.note: The infinitesimal character of a highest weight exists on the Lie-algebra side: Tau Ceti's `vermaCentralCharacter` is χ_λ : Z(U(L)) →ₐ K for a split Lie algebra in characteristic zero, the centre acts through it on every highest-weight vector of weight λ, and its Casimir value is ⟨λ+ρ,λ+ρ⟩−⟨ρ,ρ⟩. Missing: the Harish-Chandra parametrization by W-orbits under the dot action, infinitesimal characters of (g,K)-modules of a real reductive group, and cohomological representations (nonvanishing (g,K)-cohomology after twisting by a finite-dimensional representation).

targets.target: The C-algebraic vs L-algebraic normalizations and the half-root twist
targets.note: Absent; `grep -i 'algebraic'` finds no normalization convention of this kind in either tree.

targets.target: Coefficient systems from algebraic representations with lattices, independent of the lattice after inverting its primes
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Chevalley/Kostant lattice in a representation, the stable lattice such a coefficient system would use, and local coefficient systems on topological spaces (`LocalCoefficientSystem`). Nothing builds a coefficient system on an arithmetic quotient from an algebraic representation with a lattice, and there is no independence-of-lattice statement.

targets.target: Rationality and finite fields of definition for cohomological cuspidal representations
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Torsion Hecke eigenclasses defined through integral cohomology
targets.note: Absent: there is no integral cohomology of an arithmetic quotient in either library.

Constructs local systems from algebraic representations with stable lattices, the same coefficient-system target on the topological side.
Also builds coefficients from algebraic representations with the highest-weight description over a splitting field.

targets.note: `grep -rn HeckeCharacter` over both trees returns nothing: Hecke characters are not defined. Tau Ceti's multiplicative/unitary ideal weights are multiplicative functions on nonzero ideals used for L-series, the ideal-theoretic shadow of a finite-order Hecke character, and Mathlib defines the idele class group, but neither infinity types nor conductors of idele-class characters exist.

targets.target: The GL_2/Q dictionary with classical modular forms: slash actions, central character and normalized Hecke operators
targets.note: The classical side of the dictionary is fully present: Mathlib's slash action and ModularForm/CuspForm, Tau Ceti's Hecke operators with nebentypus (the central character), normalized eigenforms and coefficient formulas. The adelic side, and hence the dictionary itself, is absent.

targets.target: Algebraic modular forms on compact-at-infinity groups as functions on finite adelic double cosets valued in an algebraic representation
targets.note: Abstract double cosets and their Hecke algebra exist, but there is no finite adelic double-coset set for an algebraic group and no Gross-style algebraic modular form.

targets.target: Compatibility with restriction of scalars, products, central characters and inner forms
targets.note: Absent: there is no Weil restriction in either library (`grep -rn -i 'weil restriction'` finds nothing) and no inner form of a reductive group.

review.notes: Checked all 192 targets of the 36 layers against the roadmap extracts. All 151 distinct original citations (189 uses) resolve at their file and line in the pinned baseline and no cited file contains sorry; two were private (ModularForm.slash_mul, TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.exists_mixed_approximation) and one a deprecated alias (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.cohomologyFunctor), all replaced by public, live names. Every presence claim (5 mathlib, 29 partial) was re-read at source with its variable lines; AF.1a's continuous-cochain target was upgraded to mathlib because the differentiable complex is a separate target. More than half of the 158 absent targets, including every one with a standard Mathlib name, were re-searched by concept over declarations.tsv and both source trees, backed by five per-roadmap Explore sweeps whose proposals were opened at source before use. False or overstated absences were corrected in 38 target entries: Tau Ceti's local coefficient systems, functor of points of an affine group scheme with products, closed subgroups and centres, strong approximation for SL2 over Q, central characters of Lie algebras, continuous inflation-restriction, the Kummer map into H^1(G_K, mu_n), finite locally free group schemes with Cartier duality, toric fans, smooth discrete modules, dynamic parabolics and the E4/E6 graded ring; Mathlib's Weil formula for closed normal subgroups (Haar/Extension.lean), index-times-measure identity, test functions, Serre derivative, ell-adic cohomology of schemes and arithmetic-subgroup proper discontinuity. Five targets changed library value (four absent to partial, one partial to mathlib); no absent target became present. 15 layers marked 'partly built' had no present target and are now 'not built' (final: 3 partly built, 33 not built). All 102 duplicate claims resolve to live, non-retired stages; the hidden checkpoint BorelRegulators:KU-arithmeticgroups was replaced by its owner R.1, and 17 missed owners were added, above all the prerequisite Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology stages 4-6 for ALS.0, ALS.1, ALS.3, ALS.5 and ALS.6. After correction there are 185 distinct citations (227 uses), all resolving, none private, none in a file with sorry. The five summaries were rewritten to match. The audit's overall picture - almost nothing adelic, automorphic or Shimura-theoretic exists - stands.

corrections.why: ModularForm.slash_mul is private. The public statement is the SlashAction.slash_mul law of the anonymous instance SlashAction ℤ (GL (Fin 2) ℝ) (ℍ → ℂ) at SlashActions.lean:130, which proves it.

corrections.target: The automorphy cocycle identity j(g h, z) = j(g, h z) j(h, z) for a left action, and the derived right-action formula
corrections.was: cited the private ModularForm.slash_mul as the exact right-action formula
corrections.now: cites SlashAction.slash_mul, proved for GL(2,ℝ) by the weight-k slash-action instance
corrections.why: ModularForm.slash_mul is private, so it is not the library's statement. The public right-action law is SlashAction.slash_mul for the anonymous instance SlashAction ℤ (GL (Fin 2) ℝ) (ℍ → ℂ) at SlashActions.lean:130, whose proof is that private theorem. The target stays mathlib.

corrections.target: Generic associated-bundle construction for a torsor and a representation, with tensor products, duals, determinants and pullback
corrections.was: absent; note said no contracted product exists
corrections.now: absent; note records Tau Ceti's topological balanced product and cites it
corrections.why: TauCeti.BalancedProduct forms E ×_G A for a quotient covering map and a discrete G-set and proves the projection is a covering map with fibre A: a contracted product, though only for discrete fibres. The target (torsors under group schemes, representations, tensor operations) is still absent.

corrections.target: The local system attached to a representation of G^c, with its de Rham bundle, integrable connection and Hodge filtration
corrections.was: absent; note said there are no local systems
corrections.now: absent; note corrected and TauCeti.LocalCoefficientSystem cited
corrections.why: Tau Ceti has local coefficient systems on topological spaces (functors from the fundamental groupoid to modules). There is still no local system on a Shimura variety, no algebraic connection and no variation of Hodge structure.

corrections.target: Compatibility with refinements and independence of sections from the chosen admissible fan
corrections.was: absent; note said there is no fan theory ("Mathlib has no toric varieties")
corrections.now: absent; note records Tau Ceti's toric fans and subdivisions and cites them
corrections.why: Tau Ceti has finite rational fans with the subdivision (refinement) relation and its induced fan morphisms (TauCeti/Geometry/Toric/Algebraic/Fan). Admissible Γ-invariant cone decompositions and toroidal compactifications are still absent.

corrections.target: Identification of cuspidality with boundary vanishing
corrections.was: note said Mathlib proves cuspidality equivalent to vanishing of the constant q-coefficient, citing only one direction
corrections.now: note says the equivalence is proved at level one; ModularForm.isCuspForm_iff_coeffZero_eq_zero cited
corrections.why: CuspFormClass.qExpansion_coeff_zero is one direction for any Γ. The equivalence IsCuspForm f ↔ (qExpansion 1 f).coeff 0 = 0 is proved only for SL(2,ℤ); for general Γ the definition itself asks for vanishing at every cusp.

corrections.target: U(g_C), its centre action and generalized infinitesimal-character subspaces
corrections.was: partial; cited Subalgebra.center and the Kostant form, note said there is no description of Z(U(g)) or of central characters
corrections.now: partial; Tau Ceti's central character χ_λ : Z(U(L)) →ₐ K, its defining property and the central Casimir element cited in place of the Kostant form
corrections.why: Tau Ceti builds the central character of a weight, vermaCentralCharacter : Z(U(L)) →ₐ[K] K, proves that the centre acts on every highest-weight vector of weight λ through it, and proves the Casimir element central with value ⟨λ+ρ,λ+ρ⟩−⟨ρ,ρ⟩. That is the centre action on highest-weight modules, which the note did not record.

corrections.now: partial — Tau Ceti's central characters of weights cited
corrections.why: Tau Ceti's vermaCentralCharacter is the infinitesimal character χ_λ : Z(U(L)) →ₐ K of the highest weight λ, acting on every highest-weight vector of that weight, with its Casimir value; the infinitesimal character of an algebraic highest weight therefore exists. Cohomological representations do not.

corrections.target: Continuous group-cochain complexes for a real Lie group with finitely many components
corrections.why: This target is the continuous cochain complex alone (differentiable cochains and the smoothing comparison are the next target). Mathlib defines the homogeneous continuous cochain complex and continuous cohomology for any topological group and topological representation, which covers a real Lie group with finitely many components; the audit's own note calls it more general.
AF.3 uses "the compactness of the unipotent quotient"; its base case is exactly this Tau Ceti layer's compactness of 𝔸_K/K.
The audit cited only layer 10 (infinity types); layer 9 owns the Hecke-character carrier itself with conductor and unitary part.

corrections.target: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for each unipotent/Levi stratum
corrections.was: partial; note said there is no continuous version of inflation–restriction
corrections.now: partial; Tau Ceti's continuous degree-one inflation–restriction exactness cited and note corrected
corrections.why: TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitInfRes_exact proves exactness of H¹(G/N, M^N) → H¹(G, M) → H¹(N, M) for continuous cochains, for any topological group G and normal subgroup N, with inflation injective (explicitInfl1_injective). The continuous low-degree edge exists; the spectral sequence does not.

corrections.target: Adelic smooth test functions as a restricted tensor product of locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places and C^infty compactly supported functions at infinity
corrections.was: cited SchwartzMap for the archimedean factor
corrections.now: cites TestFunction (𝓓(Ω, F), with its LF topology) instead
corrections.why: The archimedean factor the layer asks for is C^∞ with compact support; Schwartz functions are not compactly supported. Mathlib's Analysis/Distribution/TestFunction.lean defines exactly the compactly supported smooth functions with their LF topology.

corrections.target: The complex of G-invariant V-valued differential forms on G/K
corrections.was: note said there are no differential forms on a manifold
corrections.now: note records Tau Ceti's smooth two-forms on manifolds; target stays absent
corrections.why: Tau Ceti defines smooth differential two-forms on a manifold (TauCeti.SmoothTwoForm), without an exterior derivative. Forms of all degrees with d on G/K are still absent, so only the note was inaccurate.

corrections.target: Proper discontinuity of the arithmetic action, and freeness at neat level
corrections.was: partial; cited only the discrete-subgroup-of-SL(2,ℝ) instance for the arithmetic case
corrections.now: partial; Mathlib's instance for arithmetic subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) added and note updated
corrections.why: Subgroup.IsArithmetic.properlyDiscontinuous proves that every arithmetic subgroup of GL(2,ℝ) acts properly discontinuously on ℍ: the arithmetic GL₂ case of the target itself, closer than the audit's citations.

corrections.target: Change-of-level and groupoid versions with stabilizer factors
corrections.was: absent; note said the stabilizer-weighted statement is not there
corrections.now: absent; Tau Ceti's stabilizer-weighted coset-fibre count cited and note corrected
corrections.why: TauCeti.card_fiber_orbitOfCosetTranslate_mul_cardStabilizerOnOrbit proves, for 𝒢 ≤ ℋ acting on a set, that the number of cosets of 𝒢 in ℋ carrying p into a given 𝒢-orbit times the 𝒢-stabilizer of that orbit is the ℋ-stabilizer of p: the combinatorial degree formula with stabilizer factors. It is not applied to cohomology, so the target stays absent.

corrections.target: Naturality for eligible group/coefficient maps and cup-product compatibility
corrections.was: note said Tau Ceti has the cup product on continuous cohomology, without restriction
corrections.now: note records that the Tau Ceti cup product exists only in total degree ≤ 2
corrections.why: Tau Ceti's continuous cup products (ContCohomology/Cup/Product.lean) are explicitCup00 … explicitCup20 on the explicit low-degree model; there is no cup product in all degrees. The target stays partial.

corrections.target: Restricted tensor-product factorization of irreducible admissible constituents
corrections.was: absent; note said there is no smooth representation theory of a locally profinite group
corrections.now: absent; note corrected and Tau Ceti's smooth discrete modules cited
corrections.why: TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete (discrete module, every point stabilizer open) is the smoothness condition, with an equivalence to discrete continuous modules (discreteRepEquivSmoothTopRep). There is no admissibility, restricted tensor product or Flath theorem, so the target stays absent.

corrections.target: Absence of proper rational parabolics for groups anisotropic modulo centre
corrections.was: absent; note said rational parabolics are not defined
corrections.now: absent; note records Tau Ceti's dynamic parabolics P(λ) and cites them
corrections.why: Tau Ceti defines the dynamic parabolic, Levi and unipotent subgroups of a cocharacter (TauCeti.Cocharacter.parabolic), and proves P(λ) = G for commutative groups. What is missing is F-anisotropy and the statement that every F-rational P(λ) is G for a group anisotropic modulo its centre.

corrections.target: Coefficient systems from algebraic representations with lattices, independent of the lattice after inverting its primes
corrections.was: absent; note said there is no coefficient system on a space
corrections.now: absent; note corrected and TauCeti.LocalCoefficientSystem cited
corrections.why: Tau Ceti defines local coefficient systems on topological spaces (functors from the fundamental groupoid to modules). Nothing builds one from an algebraic representation with a lattice, so the target stays absent.
ALS.0's orientation-local-system target is item 3 of this stage of the prerequisite AlgebraicTopology roadmap.
For G = GL₁ these two AA.3 targets are exactly the compactness of 𝔸¹/Kˣ and finiteness of the class group, which this layer owns.

corrections.target: Base change and restriction-of-scalars equivalences on adelic points
corrections.was: absent; note mentioned only the absence of Weil restriction
corrections.now: absent; note records the algebraic base-change identity on points and cites it
corrections.why: Tau Ceti's baseChangePointsMulEquiv identifies the A-points of a bialgebra with the R-points of its base change for every K-algebra R, the algebraic half of the base-change statement. The adelic statement still cannot be made: there is no Weil restriction and no identification 𝔸_E ≅ E ⊗ 𝔸_F.

corrections.target: Finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat levels, and degrees via stabilizer indices
corrections.was: absent; note said there is no covering-degree calculation for level subgroups
corrections.now: absent; note records the abstract covering and degree results and cites them
corrections.why: Tau Ceti proves that an intermediate quotient E/H → E/G of a quotient covering map is a covering map (IsQuotientCoveringMap.isCoveringMap_of_comp) and that the degree of a double coset H₁gH₂ is [H₁ : H₁ ∩ gH₂g⁻¹] (HeckeCoset.degree_eq_relIndex): the covering and index statements in abstract form. Neatness and adelic level quotients are still absent.

corrections.target: Comparison of volumes under finite-index level changes
corrections.was: absent; cited only the ℤ-lattice covolume/index relation
corrections.now: absent; Mathlib's index-times-measure identity for finite-index subgroups added
corrections.why: MeasureTheory.Subgroup.index_mul_measure proves [G:H]·μ(H) = μ(G) for a measurable finite-index subgroup and a left-invariant measure: the local identity vol(K) = [K:K']·vol(K') a level change uses. The adelic volume comparison is still absent.

corrections.target: Exact criterion for a coefficient to descend through the ineffective central subgroup or a finite coarse quotient
corrections.was: absent; note said there is no coarse quotient of an arithmetic quotient in either library
corrections.now: absent; note records the GL₂ analytic shadow and cites it
corrections.why: The orbit space Γ\ℍ exists and is Hausdorff for a properly discontinuous action, Mathlib proves that M_k(Γ) = 0 when −1 ∈ Γ and k is odd, and Tau Ceti proves that a form for Γ' ≤ Γ comes from Γ exactly when it is Γ-slash invariant: the central-subgroup and finite-quotient descent criteria in their analytic GL₂ form. No algebraic coarse quotient or bundle-level criterion exists.

corrections.target: Hodge-type tensor description via Betti, de Rham and étale realizations of Hodge tensors
corrections.was: absent; note said there is no étale cohomology of a variety and no Hodge tensor
corrections.now: absent; note records Mathlib's ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes and Tau Ceti's Hodge structures, and cites them
corrections.why: Mathlib defines the ℓ-adic cohomology Hⁿ(X, ℤ_ℓ) of any scheme through the pro-étale site (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EllAdicCohomology), and Tau Ceti has pure and mixed Hodge structures with tensor products, duals and internal Hom. There are still no Hodge tensors, Mumford–Tate groups, de Rham realizations or comparison isomorphisms.

corrections.target: Composition against the existing abstract Hecke algebra, with all scalar normalizations
corrections.was: partial; note said nothing acts through the abstract Hecke algebra
corrections.now: partial; Tau Ceti's ring homomorphism from the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring to endomorphisms of M_k(N, χ) cited
corrections.why: HeckeRing.GL2.heckeRingHomCharSpace is a ring homomorphism 𝕋(Δ₀(N), Γ₀(N)) ℤ →+* End_ℂ(M_k(Γ₁(N), χ)): composition against the abstract Hecke ring, with its normalizations, for analytic GL₂ forms. It does not act on bundle sections, so the target stays partial.

corrections.was: said there is no functor of points G(𝔸), no strong approximation for any algebraic group, and that Mathlib has the Weil formula only for a discrete subgroup
corrections.why: Tau Ceti has the functor of points of an affine group scheme (evaluable on the adele ring) and strong approximation for SL₂ over ℚ; Mathlib has Weil's formula for closed normal subgroups in Haar/Extension.lean.

corrections.was: did not mention the level-one graded ring, the Serre derivative, Tau Ceti's finite locally free group schemes or its Kummer theory
corrections.why: These are present at the pin and are the nearest carriers for R15.2, R15.3 and R15.4; the target-level corrections record them.

corrections.was: listed local systems among the absent geometry and did not name the prerequisite AlgebraicTopology stages
corrections.why: Tau Ceti defines local coefficient systems (TauCeti.LocalCoefficientSystem) and continuous inflation–restriction, and the roadmap's own prerequisite tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicTopology owns the singular cochain, cellular and duality theory ALS.1–ALS.6 restate.

corrections.was: did not mention Tau Ceti's local coefficient systems, Hodge structures, toric fans or balanced products
corrections.why: These exist at the pin and bear on B0, B1–B2 and B3; the target-level corrections cite them.

corrections.was: said Tau Ceti has no infinitesimal characters and called continuous cochains only the first half of AF.1a
corrections.why: Tau Ceti's vermaCentralCharacter is the infinitesimal character of a highest weight; Mathlib's continuous cochain complex is the whole of AF.1a's continuous-cochain target (the differentiable complex is a separate target).
